Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Church life · Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

religious adjective

to do with religion and worship

also religious matters, religious ceremony, religious book, sacred

classical

Cic. Div. 2.10; Liv. 23.11 (Lewis & Short)
Caes. BG 6.13.4: rēbus dīvīnīs intersunt

rēs dīvīnae

rēs, reī f., with dīvīnus; also singular, rēs dīvīna, a service or sacrifice

religious matters; worship

Religious, as against secular, business: the plural for religious matters in general, the singular rēs dīvīna for an act of worship (Lewis & Short: “very freq.” in Plautus and Terence). With other nouns Latin usually says sacer.

Other words

  • sacer, sacra, sacrum — sacred, holy; dedicated to God (the gods)

    also used · classical · Cic. Verr. 2.4.129: pūblicīs prīvātīs sacrīs profānīs (Lewis & Short)

    Consecrated to the divine, as against profānus, not consecrated (Lewis & Short); so a religious building is aedificium sacrum. As a noun, sacra are rites and sacred things.

Examples

  • aedificiīs omnibus, pūblicīs prīvātīs sacrīs profānīs, sīc pepercit

    he spared all the buildings, public and private, religious and secular alikeCic. Verr. 2.4.129 (Lewis & Short)

  • illī rēbus dīvīnīs intersunt, sacrificia pūblica ac prīvāta prōcūrant, religiōnēs interpretantur

    they take part in worship, look after the sacrifices of the state and of private people, and interpret religious questionsCaes. BG 6.13.4

See also religion, religious, church.

SourcesLewis & Short: divinus · Lewis & Short: sacer

Caesar (BG 6.13.4) quoted as in the record national.

Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, with its references, in the house spelling (macrons, consonantal j); they have not been checked against a modern edition.
